findings.reason: the plan must name the interface change (open resolves a directory/layout, or transform_machine_description pre-resolves the map directory) or the extension it claims is not implementable as drawn.
findings.text: §4 claims it "extends that engine" so a store "declared static over its map resolves {root}/{map name} and reads one {ids}.nc per IDS", but the engine it must extend, NetCDFTransformEngine.open(root, shot, dd_version), unconditionally appends str(int(shot)) and never receives the map; transform_machine_description:384 holds the catalogue and map_for_shot:375 but the interface carries no way to select the static layout, so the plan's new addressing cannot be hidden behind the current open()

findings.reason: the plan should name the eligibility and minimum-shot parameters the loader boundary must also expose, or SELENE/FAME cannot reuse it as claimed.
findings.text: §6 says it generalises measure_diiid_convention "to take an equilibrium record through a loader" leaving only a "record contract with canonical keys for the grid, psi, axis and boundary", but the kernel's entrypoint also hard-codes DIII-D eligibility (MINIMUM_PLASMA_CURRENT_KA=500.0, STANDARD_FIELD_BCOIL_MAXIMUM=0.0 at convention.py:38-40) and the MINIMUM_AUDIT_SHOTS=20 guard at :264; a loader seam over those leaves SELENE/FAME unable to pass the entrypoint, and _axis_and_boundary also needs grid_Z and the lcfs arrays, not only grid/psi/axis/boundary

— §7 asserts "the selector therefore takes the machine from the catalogue the shot belongs to and passes it to the identity registry", but the shot→machine owner, identity_for_shot, resolves through default_registry() (machine_identity.py:145), fixed to Nova's MAST geometry registry, and takes a registry object rather than a machine; no file maps a shot to a catalogue (map_for_shot:1534 selects a map within one catalogue), and open question jt60sa-artifact-authoring leaves unresolved whether Nova can materialise a JT-60SA artifact for that registry at all; WOULD_CHANGE_THE_PLAN: yes — REASON: the plan must name the owner to extend for shot→machine resolution (default_registry / the identity registry) and reconcile it with the unresolved artifact-authoring question, or the §7 selection path has no owner to extend.

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — the §4 "static over its map" store layout cannot be hidden behind the existing engine interface, which carries no map.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §7 presumes a shot→catalogue resolver and a per-machine identity registry that no file owns; the owner to extend is gs/machine_identity.identity_for_shot / default_registry.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; every section that adds surface states its retirement in its own text (§2 "retires nothing, because ambix has no exporter"; §3 "retires nothing, because ambix has no remote reader today ... adds no ambix data command"; §4 "retires nothing inside ambix, because ambix has no deck reader today ... the probe-angle key retires the machine branch"; §7 "adds two record fields and retires nothing, because no scalar reference comparison exists yet").
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan names and I verified each owner it extends (cocos_convention.score_convention, challenge/convention._integrated_current, eval/efit_referee.judge_geometry, description_identity, gs/artifact_resolution, imas_codex remote layer) and cites codex's remote scripts rather than presenting them as absent.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — the §6 loader seam is thin over a kernel whose surrounding entrypoint stays DIII-D-specific, so the reuse it promises is incomplete.
